_provenance: NOAA CPC official seasonal precipitation outlook legend (cpc.ncep.noaa.gov/products/predictions/long_range/lead02/off02_prcp.gif, sampled from the September 2026 issue): 'Above Normal' greens and 'Below Normal' browns in seven bands 33-40 % (leaning), 40-50, 50-60 (likely), 60-70, 70-80, 80-90, 90-100; 'Near Normal' greys, of which CPC draws only 33-40 and 40-50 -- the five darker greys here extend that ramp so the style is well-formed and are not reached in practice; 'Equal Chances' white. Which cells are white follows the CAPC-AC display rule inherited from CPC's NMME tercile summary (cpc.ncep.noaa.gov/products/NMME/NMME_PROB_descr.html): an outer tercile is shown only where the opposite outer tercile is under 33 % (secondary_max), a leading near-normal needs both outer terciles under 33 %; a contested cell is white (equal chances). The leading category is banded from 33.3 % as in CPC's legend; the earlier 38 % leading floor of the noaa-nmme style (this style's former name) is gone. Dry season in grey.
